A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EDLM work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–D are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original EDLM language-modeling and generation results in Tables 1–3, sampling ablations, and appendix analyses and generated examples.

after.justification: v2 retains the original EDLM experiments, including benchmark results, sampling ablations, energy-function analyses, and generated examples.

M1.justification: The residual energy model, AR/coAR and NCE variants, training objective, and Algorithms 1–2 are retained. The revised Equation 11 changes the mathematical exposition of denoising without establishing a different implemented procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use Text8 and OpenWebText, evaluate zero-shot perplexity on the same seven additional datasets, and retain the same unconditional-generation scenarios. No dataset or task coverage is added.

E2.justification: MD4 (Shi et al., 2024) is added to the Text8 comparison in Table 1. v1 cited this work but omitted it from that comparison. Comparator membership in Tables 2–3 remains unchanged.

E3.justification: The stated datasets, splits, metrics, architectures, training budgets, and evaluation procedures are retained. Section 5.3 newly specifies k = 2 for the existing speed experiment; v1 left this unspecified, so this is additional documentation rather than an established protocol change.

E4.justification: Figure 3 revises the window-length sensitivity results by reversing the window values assigned to the existing curves. Other ablations, energy/ESS analyses, and generated examples are retained. New Figure 4 explicitly redisplays existing results rather than introducing another experiment.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The partition-function estimators and appendix ESS analysis remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds MD4 at BPC ≤1.37; EDLM remains ≤1.24. Figure 3 changes the window assignments for unchanged curves from 0.8/0.6/0.4/0.2 to 0.2/0.4/0.6/0.8. Tables 2–3 and the proposed models' benchmark scores are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equation 11 replaces the piecewise categorical substitution with an expectation over the joint x0 distribution and a marginal probability for revealed tokens. This is a localized revision of the formal denoising expression; Theorem 1 and its Appendix A proof are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and performance claims: sequence-level energy correction, approaching autoregressive perplexity, and up to 1.3× sampling speedup.

C2.justification: Section 2 newly argues that reranking/remasking can bias sampling and reduce diversity, explaining its distinction from distribution modeling. Appendix C.2 otherwise reiterates the existing interpretation that EDLM reaches a similar quality/diversity tradeoff with fewer sampling steps.

D1.justification: Section 5.3 newly discloses importance-sampling size k = 2 for the timing experiment, alongside the retained window w = 0.2. The new reproducibility statement mainly points to existing algorithms and implementation details; Appendix C.1 is unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 expands comparisons with autoregressive residual EBMs and non-autoregressive reranking/remasking approaches. Four references are added: Gu et al. (2018), Ghazvininejad et al. (2019), Gu and Kong (2021), and Zheng et al. (2023).

P1.justification: v2 adds short related-work and appendix explanations, a reproducibility statement, and acknowledgments, with small terminology and author-contact edits. The main narrative and section organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure 4 by replotting Figures 1a–b against entropy and generative perplexity, revises Figure 3's legends, and adds a Table 1 row. Conference headers and limited text reflow accompany these changes.

improvement.justification: The added MD4 comparison, disclosed k = 2 timing setting, and corrected Figure 3 window labels improve completeness, reproducibility, and interpretability. Figure 4 makes the existing quality/diversity tradeoff easier to assess. These are useful but limited refinements; the core method, main experimental results, and conclusions remain stable.
